biomarkers.description: Primary iron-containing metalloprotein in erythrocytes responsible for intravascular molecular oxygen transport from lungs to peripheral tissues.

fasting_requirements.details: Fasting not physiologically required for standard Complete Blood Count.

measurement_context.methodology: Automated blood cell analyzer (SLS-hemoglobin or cyanmethemoglobin method)

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult Non-Pregnant Males (Biological Sex-Stratified; subject to local laboratory platform calibration)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry (6th Ed.) / MedlinePlus (2024)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Reference intervals vary with local analyzer instrumentation, patient smoking status, and geographical altitude.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult Non-Pregnant Females (Biological Sex-Stratified; subject to local laboratory platform calibration)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry (6th Ed.) / MedlinePlus (2024)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: In pregnant patients, physiological hemodilution lowers reference limits (1st trimester: 11.0; 2nd trimester: 10.5; 3rd trimester: 11.0 g/dL).

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.condition_name: Anemia (WHO Epidemiological Diagnostic Criterion - Adult Male)
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: Hemoglobin < 13.0 g/dL defines anemia in adult men. Serves as clinical diagnostic criterion; underlying etiology (iron deficiency, chronic disease, hemolysis, hemoglobinopathy) must be established by further clinical investigation.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: WHO Haemoglobin concentrations for the diagnosis of anaemia and assessment of severity (2011)

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.condition_name: Anemia (WHO Epidemiological Diagnostic Criterion - Non-Pregnant Adult Female)
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: Hemoglobin < 12.0 g/dL defines anemia in non-pregnant adult women. Warrants clinical evaluation of iron stores and red cell indices.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: WHO Haemoglobin concentrations for the diagnosis of anaemia and assessment of severity (2011)

critical_laboratory_limits.clinical_urgency: Urgent notification limit: High risk of tissue hypoxia (< 7.0 g/dL; common transfusion consideration trigger in hemodynamically stable patients per AABB guidelines) or severe hyperviscosity (> 20.0 g/dL). Does not mandate automatic transfusion; clinical context governs all decisions.
critical_laboratory_limits.source_reference: Massachusetts General Hospital Laboratory Handbook / Kost Critical Limits Consensus Survey
critical_laboratory_limits.institutional_note: Institutional panic value policy. MGH sets panic limits at < 7.0 g/dL and > 20.0 g/dL. Surveys by Kost (Am J Clin Pathol 1990) show multi-institutional consensus panic ranges of 6.6-7.0 g/dL (low) and 19.9-20.0 g/dL (high). Exact notification cutoffs depend on local laboratory SOP.

provenance.primary_document_title: Haemoglobin concentrations for the diagnosis of anaemia and assessment of severity
provenance.clinical_notes: Diagnostic threshold for anemia differs from general hospital statistical reference intervals.

biomarkers.description: Total concentration of circulating erythrocytes per unit volume of whole blood.

measurement_context.methodology: Hydrodynamic focusing and electrical impedance / flow cytometry

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult Males (Biological Sex-Stratified; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Depends on altitude, hydration status, and analyzer calibration.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult Females (Biological Sex-Stratified; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Lower ranges observed during normal pregnancy due to plasma expansion.

provenance.clinical_notes: Counts vary with high altitude acclimatization and hydration status.

biomarkers.description: Total circulating leukocyte concentration defending against biological infection, inflammation, and cellular debris.

measurement_context.methodology: Automated hematology analyzer using impedance, optical scatter, or fluorescence flow cytometry

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adults (All Genders; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: MedlinePlus / Tietz Clinical Guide to Laboratory Tests
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Significant diurnal variation (higher in afternoon) and acute increases with physical exercise, stress, and corticosteroid therapy.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.condition_name: SIRS (Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome) Leukocyte Criterion
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: WBC > 12000 /uL or < 4000 /uL or > 10% immature band forms represents one component criterion for SIRS. Does not autonomously diagnose sepsis or infection without appropriate clinical evaluation.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: American College of Chest Physicians / Society of Critical Care Medicine (ACCP/SCCM)

critical_laboratory_limits.clinical_urgency: Urgent alert: Severe opportunistic infection risk (< 2000 /uL) or leukemoid reaction / severe hematologic abnormality (> 30000 /uL). Prompts urgent clinician notification.
critical_laboratory_limits.source_reference: Kost Laboratory Critical Limits Survey / CAP Q-Probes
critical_laboratory_limits.institutional_note: Established via national surveys of US hospital panic policies (Kost, Am J Clin Pathol 1990; CAP Q-Probes). Median low threshold: 2,000 /uL (range 1,500-2,500 /uL); median high threshold: 30,000 /uL (range 25,000-50,000 /uL). Subject to institutional laboratory policy.

provenance.clinical_notes: Physical exertion, corticosteroid administration, and acute stress transiently elevate WBC counts.

biomarkers.description: Circulating anucleate cellular fragments derived from bone marrow megakaryocytes essential for primary hemostatic plug formation.

measurement_context.methodology: Automated blood cell analyzer (electrical impedance or optical scatter)

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adults (All Genders; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: MedlinePlus / AACC Laboratory Reference Range Guide
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Slightly lower counts may be observed in healthy individuals of certain demographic backgrounds (e.g., Mediterranean ancestry) without clinical bleeding risk.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: Platelet count < 150000 /uL defines thrombocytopenia. Underlying cause (immune, drug-induced, consumption, sequestration) requires clinical investigation. EDTA pseudothrombocytopenia must be ruled out.

critical_laboratory_limits.clinical_urgency: Urgent alert: Spontaneous bleeding risk (< 50000 /uL; extreme life-threatening intracranial risk < 20000 /uL) or thrombotic complications / extreme thrombocytosis (> 1000000 /uL). Warrants urgent clinician review.
critical_laboratory_limits.source_reference: CAP Critical Values / Massachusetts General Hospital Handbooks
critical_laboratory_limits.institutional_note: Institutional panic limit policy. MGH sets critical notification threshold at < 50,000 /uL (and > 1,000,000 /uL). For outpatient clinics, some hospital laboratories use < 20,000 /uL as the emergency panic cutoff. Determined by individual hospital laboratory medical director.

provenance.clinical_notes: EDTA-induced platelet clumping must be ruled out via peripheral smear review.

biomarkers.description: Average physical volume and size of individual circulating red blood cells, calculated as (Hematocrit x 10) / RBC.

measurement_context.methodology: Directly derived from red cell volume distribution pulse heights in analyzer

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adults (All Genders; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: MedlinePlus / Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Pediatric cohorts have substantially lower MCV values (e.g. 70-86 fL in young children).

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: MCV < 80 fL indicates microcytic red blood cell lineage. Serves as morphological classification directing differential diagnostic workup (e.g., ferritin testing for iron deficiency, hemoglobin electrophoresis for thalassemia). Does not constitute an autonomous diagnosis of iron deficiency.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: British Society for Haematology (BSH) Guidelines for the Investigation of Iron Deficiency

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: MCV > 100 fL indicates macrocytic red blood cell lineage. Directs differential diagnostic workup (e.g., serum B12, folate, reticulocyte count, thyroid panel). Does not constitute an autonomous diagnosis of megaloblastic anemia.

provenance.clinical_notes: MCV serves as an essential branching parameter for morphologic evaluation of anemia.

biomarkers.description: Average mass of hemoglobin contained inside an individual red blood cell, calculated as (Hemoglobin x 10) / RBC.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adults (All Genders; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: MedlinePlus / Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Depends directly on precision of hemoglobin and red cell count measurements.

provenance.clinical_notes: Parallels MCV; decreased in hypochromic anemias.

biomarkers.description: Average concentration of hemoglobin in a given volume of packed red blood cells, calculated as (Hemoglobin / Hematocrit) x 100.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adults (All Genders; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: Tietz Clinical Guide to Laboratory Tests (4th Ed.) / MedlinePlus
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Analytical quality control parameter; tightly regulated physiologically.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.condition_name: Hereditary Spherocytosis / Cold Agglutinin Evaluation Criterion
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: MCHC > 36.0 g/dL indicates potential erythrocyte dehydration, hereditary spherocytosis, or laboratory artifact (cold agglutinin agglutination, lipemia, hemolysis). Directs laboratory investigation, not an autonomous diagnosis.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: International Council for Standardization in Haematology (ICSH)

provenance.primary_source_organization: International Council for Standardization in Haematology / MedlinePlus
provenance.primary_document_title: ICSH recommendations for the analysis of red blood cells
provenance.clinical_notes: Serves as a crucial analytical quality check on hematology instrumentation.

biomarkers.description: Volume fraction of whole blood composed of packed erythrocytes.

measurement_context.methodology: Automated calculation as (RBC * MCV) / 10; or microhematocrit centrifugation

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult Males (Biological Sex-Stratified; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: MedlinePlus / Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Lower values observed in patients with fluid overload or recumbent position.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult Females (Biological Sex-Stratified; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: MedlinePlus / Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Significantly drops during second and third trimesters of pregnancy due to hemodilution (normal 30-38%).

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: Hematocrit > 49% in men or > 48% in women serves as one of three major diagnostic criteria for polycythemia vera per WHO classification. Confirmed diagnosis requires meeting additional criteria (e.g., JAK2 mutation, bone marrow biopsy).
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016 / 2022 Update)

critical_laboratory_limits.clinical_urgency: Urgent alert: Severe decompensated anemia / heart failure danger (< 21%) or dangerous hyperviscosity / spontaneous thrombotic event risk (> 60%). Warrants immediate physician communication.
critical_laboratory_limits.source_reference: CAP Critical Values Survey / Hospital Reference Policies
critical_laboratory_limits.institutional_note: CAP survey of panic limits indicates median low cutoff of 20-21% and median high cutoff of 60%. Institutional thresholds range from 18-24% (low) and 54-65% (high) depending on inpatient vs. outpatient population.

provenance.clinical_notes: Corresponds closely to 3x hemoglobin in normocytic normochromic samples.
